# Communicating results
    
Week 9 tutorial goals:
  * Regression tables
  * Model predictions -- `plot_predictions()`
  * Save tables and figures

## Set-up
```{r,include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(haven)
library(modelsummary)
library(marginaleffects)
options(warn = -1) # suppress warning messages that do not disturb the program flow
```



## Load libraries
```{r,eval=F}
library(tidyverse)
library(haven)

install.packages("modelsummary") # regression table
install.packages("pandoc") # to save regression table to Word doc output
library(modelsummary)

install.packages("marginaleffects") # model predictions
library(marginaleffects)
```


## VDem

```{r}
vars <- c("country_name", "country_id", "year", 
          "v2x_corr","e_gdppc")

vdem_2009 <- read.csv("Project/VDem/vdem2000_2023.csv") |>
  dplyr::select(all_of(vars)) |>
  filter(year==2009) 
```


### Scatter plot the bivariate relationship {-}
```{r}
ggplot(data=vdem_2009,aes(x=v2x_corr,y=e_gdppc)) +
  geom_point()
```

### Regression line {-}
```{r}
ggplot(data=vdem_2009,aes(x=v2x_corr,y=e_gdppc)) +
  geom_point(size=1,alpha=.5) +
  geom_smooth(method="lm",size=.5) + # linear model, i.e. linear regression
  scale_y_continuous(breaks=c(seq(-5,100,by=10)))
```

#### Save ggplot as object {-}
```{r}
corruption_plot <- ggplot(data=vdem_2009,aes(x=v2x_corr,y=e_gdppc)) + # assign ggplot to corruption_plot
  geom_point(size=1,alpha=.5) +
  geom_smooth(method="lm",size=.5) + # linear model, i.e. linear regression
  scale_y_continuous(breaks=c(seq(-5,100,by=10)))
```

#### Using `ggsave` {-}
```{r}
# specify arguments `filename`, `plot`, `width` and `height` of image file
ggsave(filename = "regressionLine.png",
       plot = corruption_plot,
       width=8, height=5)
```


### Regression table {-}

#### Table using `modelsummary` {-}
```{r}
corruption_model <- lm(data=vdem_2009,e_gdppc ~ v2x_corr)

modelsummary(corruption_model, stars=TRUE)
```

Now interpret: what does this mean?

#### Goodness-of-fit statistics {-}
```{r}
get_gof(corruption_model)
```

#### Select relevant statistics {-}

* Keep only "number of observations", "R-squared", and "adjusted R-squared" values
```{r}
modelsummary(corruption_model, 
             stars=TRUE, 
             gof_map=c("nobs","r.squared","adj.r.squared")) # select relevant goodness-of-fit statistics
```

#### Relabel {-}
```{r}
modelsummary(list("Base"=corruption_model), # list allows me to name the models
             stars=TRUE,
             gof_map=c("nobs","r.squared","adj.r.squared"), 
             coef_rename=c("v2x_corr"="Corruption Index")) # rename coefficient
```


#### Save output {-}
Under Arguments > output, you can see a number of supported file formats: .docx, .html, .tex, .md, .txt, .csv, .xlsx, .png, .jpg
```{r}
?modelsummary
```


```{r,eval=F}
modelsummary(list("Base"=corruption_model),
             stars=TRUE,
             gof_map=c("nobs","r.squared","adj.r.squared"), 
             coef_rename=c("v2x_corr"="Corruption Index"),
             output="out.docx") 
```

### Clear environment {-}
```{r}
rm(list=ls())
```


## Canadian Election Study 2025

```{r}
vars <- c("cps25_age_in_years","cps25_news_cons","cps25_govt_confusing") #news consumption and internal political efficacy

ces_select <- read_dta("Project/CES2025/2025 Canadian Election Study v1.dta") |>
  dplyr::select(all_of(vars))
```

### Transform & drop NAs {-}
```{r}
ces_dropna <- ces_select |>
  mutate(cps25_govt_confusing=ifelse(cps25_govt_confusing==5, #conditional statement
                                     NA, #if yes
                                     cps25_govt_confusing), #if no
         cps25_news_cons=ifelse(cps25_news_cons==7, #conditional statement
                                NA, #if yes
                                cps25_news_cons)) |> #if no
  na.omit() #remove NAs
```

### Check transformed variables {-}
```{r}
table(ces_dropna$cps25_govt_confusing)

table(ces_dropna$cps25_news_cons)
```


### Regression table {-}
```{r}
news_model <- lm(data=ces_dropna,cps25_govt_confusing ~ cps25_news_cons) # model 1

modelsummary(list("Base"=news_model),
             stars=TRUE,
             gof_map=c("nobs","r.squared","adj.r.squared"),
             coef_rename=c("cps25_news_cons"="News Consumption"))
```

Now interpret: what does this mean?

#### Controls {-}
```{r}
news_age_model <- lm(data=ces_dropna,cps25_govt_confusing ~ cps25_news_cons + cps25_age_in_years) # model 2

modelsummary(list("Base" = news_model,
                  "w/ Controls" = news_age_model),
             stars=TRUE,
             gof_map=c("nobs","r.squared","adj.r.squared"), 
             coef_rename=c("cps25_news_cons" = "News Consumption",
                           "cps25_age_in_years" = "Age"))
```

Now interpret: what does this mean?

### Model predictions -- `plot_predictions()` {-}

`plot_predictions()` from the package `marginaleffects` shows the predicted value of the dependent variable at each value of the independent variable. The `condition` argument is the variable on the x-axis.
```{r}
plot_predictions(news_model, condition = "cps25_news_cons")
```

The same plot for the model with controls.
```{r}
plot_predictions(news_age_model, condition = "cps25_news_cons")
```

Now interpret: what does this mean?

#### Save output {-}
```{r,eval=F}
modelsummary(list("Base" = news_model,
                  "w/ Controls" = news_age_model),
             stars=TRUE,
             gof_map=c("nobs","r.squared","adj.r.squared"), 
             coef_rename=c("cps25_news_cons" = "News Consumption",
                           "cps25_age_in_years" = "Age"),
             output="ces.docx") 
```

### Clear environment {-}
```{r}
rm(list=ls())
```
